# Scenarios — what each one proves

Each `lisp/<name>/` dir is one differential scenario: `s.json` drives `near-mock`
(manifest → contracts, steps with byte-exact storage asserts). Oracle values
come from `proof/pins*.json` — generated by `generators/gen*.py` from the same
constants the contracts were built with. `ts/<name>/` is the same scenario
rerun against the TS twins (fresh state every run).

`state.bin` = chain state left by the last run (regenerable; additive-ledger
pitfall documented in `../README.md` — `make clean` purges).

## Leg 2+3 — pairwise theory pins (regenerated by `proof/run_scen.py`)

Every scenario swaps the *same* amount through different routes and asserts
byte-exact `paid:` totals on each:

| scenario | route comparison | pins |
|---|---|---|
| `exact` | `join-ab` vs `pool-a` direct vs `split-ab` | amount lands exactly ON a grid point — gross/net bookkeeping at boundary |
| `offgrid` | same routes | amount lands strictly inside an interval |
| `cross` | same routes, big amount | multi-cell walk across grid cells |
| `inside` | pools with `start` mid-interval | interior entry = the refine/slice identity (refined pool ≡ original from that price) |
| `join` | `fee-join-ac` vs `pool-a`+`pool-c` legs | heterogeneous-fee pool_fee_join theorem (QBK = QA+QC exact; Fhat per cell) |
| `inside-join` | fee-join routes, interior entry | same theorem with `start` mid-interval |

## Leg 2 — splitter optimality (`opt-*`)

`opt-exact` / `opt-cross` / `opt-offgrid`: swap hand-picked alternative splits
through `pool-a`/`pool-b` directly, then run the same budget through
`split-ab` — the splitter's equalized-ending-price routing must match/beat
every alternative (concavity ⇒ equalize ending price is optimal). The three
variants land exact-boundary / multi-cell / interior respectively.

## Leg 4 — N=3 composition (static `s.json` from `generators/gen3.py` era)

All drive `split-3` over pools `pa`+`n1`+`n2`; they differ by budget regime,
forcing different active sets in the equal-price solution:

| scenario | regime |
|---|---|
| `npool-star` | budget reaches all three pools — fully equalized |
| `npool-two` | search collapses to two pools (n2 attach 0 — the ERR_ZERO path) |
| `npool-over` / `npool-under` | over / under the equalization threshold boundary |
| `opt-n` | the headline counterexample: all-in on n2 (least liquidity) nets LESS than the composed optimum — why composition exists |

`get-paid`/`get-split` steps assert the splitter's routing + receipts exactly.
